visual: Fern-like cut foliage · brilliant orange-red autumn colour · crimson fruit cones
soilWarning: Full sun for strongest autumn colour
prune: Remove unwanted suckers in winter; prune only if needed
hardinessNote: RHS H6 for the exact cultivar
resilience: cold hardy · exposed-site tolerant · generally pest free
uncertain: RHS accepts Rhus typhina 'Dissecta' and lists Rhus typhina f. laciniata and 'Laciniata' as synonyms
Kew treats both f. laciniata and f. dissecta as synonyms of Rhus typhina rather than accepted infraspecific taxa
the plant suckers vigorously and can become a garden nuisance, but no current England and Wales statutory invasive-plant restriction was verified
toxicity information is conflicting between secondary sources; authoritative horticultural sources do not support a clear customer toxicity warning, so toxicity is left blank
spread can approach 6 m or more because of the naturally broad, suckering habit
peak represents the principal autumn foliage and fruit display rather than flowering
